comment: Narrowed (lab-c, round 2). The model.py accepts only pairwise separations within 0.05 of 5.0 (abs(sep - R0) > 0.05 raises). The claims state 3.75-5.0 (c2) and 4.5-5.5 (c1), so the model does not predict those ranges. 2026-11-20/r1/lab-c/011 (side 4.5) and 012 (side 4.0) are refused by it, so the judge cannot score them against P-0007. I cite them for the physics only: they match P-0008's pair law at tracker noise (judged 0.0073 and 0.0072). Endpoint evidence the model does accept: 2026-11-19/r3/lab-c/001 (A, A, A, side 5.0, T=1.5) at judged 0.0069, with per-particle residual rms 0.042-0.053 per coordinate and zero-force null 0.22 (analysis/p0007_c2_check.py); 2026-11-19/r1/lab-c/020 (A, B, C, side 5.0, T=2) at 0.0072. The physics is consistent with my data at sides 4.0-5.0; the defect is the model's domain. Recommend either making model.py accept the stated range or narrowing the statement to separations 4.95-5.05, as proposed. No in-domain c1 run of mine exists apart from the endpoint. The judged metric (RMSE/10) sits at the noise floor (0.0071) and does not resolve a few-percent coupling error.
